title: Fix the data race
description:
`Counter::increment` is called by many threads at once. `++m_value` looks like one step but is three (read, add, write), and two threads can interleave so that one increment is lost. The test runs 8 threads × 20,000 increments and, without protection, comes up short.

Protect the counter with a `std::mutex`. Lock it in `increment` and in `value` using `std::lock_guard`, which unlocks automatically when it goes out of scope. The mutex must be `mutable` so that the `const` function `value()` can lock it too.
hints: Add `mutable std::mutex m_mutex;` to the class. In both functions, the first line is `std::lock_guard lock{ m_mutex };`; the lock is released when the function returns.
rules: Lock it with an RAII lock, not by calling `lock()` and `unlock()` yourself.

rules.message: Lock it with an RAII lock, not by calling `lock()` and `unlock()` yourself.
